summary: Discusses using IPv6 /127 prefix lengths on point-to-point router links. Because of subnet-router anycast, one router might claim both addresses, and the document explains the problem and offers a couple of solutions, while advising that /127 be avoided between two routers. It is historic and has been replaced by RFC 6547.

eli5.summary: A tiny two-seat bench is too small if the bench itself counts as a seat that one person may grab. This says do not carve router links that tightly. The advice has since been replaced by RFC 6547.

questions: is /127 ok for ipv6 point to point links
